html:
SMTO-EXE-0268 — A workflow step may already have made its change

GUID: 9f995161-8187-54bc-94c4-570702d76ac3
Slug: recipe-step-outcome-unknown
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: recipes

What happened

  • SMTO lost track of whether a workflow step finished, or an earlier run of this workflow is still open. The change may already have happened, so SMTO is blocking further changes until that's checked.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the conversation of the workflow's latest run, for example from History with Open run, and find the step marked uncertain or still running. That step is the one SMTO can't confirm.
  2. Check the result yourself, for example look at the file, message or record that step was changing, or ask SMTO in that conversation to check it without changing anything. Looking is safe; doing the step again could make the change twice.
  3. Tell SMTO in that conversation whether the change is in place. Only if it didn't happen, ask SMTO to do that one step. This settles the uncertain step so the workflow can continue from the right point.
  4. If an earlier run is still going, wait for it to finish, or stop it from its conversation, before starting a new run. SMTO won't start a new run while an earlier one may still be changing things.

What success looks like

  • The run's conversation shows no uncertain or running steps, and a new run can start.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the workflow's name and what you found, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't start the workflow again or repeat the step until you know whether the change already happened.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Recorded-workflow execution is blocked because an earlier run is pending, running or unsettled, a step is running or outcome_unknown, or a result cannot prove whether the write took effect.

What this means

  • A prior workflow run is pending/running or unsettled, a step is running/unknown, or a receipt cannot prove a successful or definitely unexecuted effect. Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.

Why this can happen

  • A prior workflow run is pending/running or unsettled, a step is running/unknown, or a receipt cannot prove a successful or definitely unexecuted effect.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original operation identities, receipts and current resource state; only supported adapter-owned reconciliation can establish completion.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the recipe's runs (agent_recipe_runs status and metadata step_states) and the task's recipe_steps and unknown_operations (store.create_run, runtime.guard, runtime.observe). Settle each uncertain write by reading the target's current state and recording the outcome; never restart the workflow or replay the write.
  • Reconcile the original work with fresh reads and supported evidence; do not restart the workflow or replay uncertain writes.

Retry and execution caution

  • Reconcile the original work with fresh reads and supported evidence; do not restart the workflow or replay uncertain writes.

How to verify the fix

  • Uncertain effects are settled with valid evidence before any dependent mutation is admitted.

What not to do

  • Never repeat a write whose effect remains unknown.

Technical notes

  • Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
